## Builtins (343)

| Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Chan::new(capacity: i64) -> Chan<i64>` | Create a new channel. `capacity` is accepted but not enforced — the buffer grows (spec phase-3 §4), the same as the `chan<T>()` spelling. Interpreter-only. |
| `E(dist: Any) -> f64` | Phase 13 Slice 2: E[dist] — expected value (mean) of a distribution in a refinement predicate. |
| `P(event: bool) -> f64` | Phase 13 Slice 2: P(dist op k) — tail probability of a distribution in a refinement predicate. |
| `Var(dist: Any) -> f64` | Phase 13 Slice 2: Var[dist] — variance of a distribution in a refinement predicate. |
| `abs_f64(n: f64) -> f64` | Absolute value of an `f64`. |
| `abs_i32(n: i64) -> i32` | Absolute value of an integer (truncated to i32 range). |
| `abs_i64(n: i64) -> i64` | Absolute value of an i64. |
| `agent_detect_loop(name: str) -> bool` | Metacognition: has the agent's reasoning STALLED? True when the last few recorded scores for `name` are all within an epsilon of each other (no progress — a likely reasoning loop). False with fewer than 3 records (not enough trace to judge). Reads the same trace as `goal_history`. |
| `agent_trace_len(name: str) -> i64` | Metacognition: the number of reasoning steps (recorded scores) in the agent's trace for `name` — the length of its `reasoning_trace()`. 0 when nothing recorded. |
| `agent_uncertainty(name: str) -> f64` | Metacognition: the agent's self-estimated uncertainty in `[0,1]`, derived from the spread of its recent scores (normalized stdev — high variance ⇒ high uncertainty). Returns 1.0 (maximally uncertain) when fewer than 2 records exist. The PRD's `uncertainty_estimate()` as a trace-backed scalar. |
| `ai_complete(prompt: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Send prompt to the Anthropic API (claude-sonnet-4-6) and return the reply. Returns Ok(reply) or Err(message). Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var. |
| `ai_cost_spent() -> i64` | Phase-7 cost_meter / F4: cumulative AI spend so far this run, in integer micro-dollars (µ$). Every dispatched `ai_complete` (mock or live) adds its per-token cost (tier rate × estimated tokens); an offline fallback adds nothing. The kernel cost meter that `llm_gateway.ax` modeled — read it to gate on a real cost budget (distinct from R3c's per-call-count `@[ai(policy(budget:N))]`). Deterministic, so it works under AXON_AI_MOCK. |
| `ai_extract_uncertain_f64(prompt: str) -> Result<Uncertain<f64>, str>` | Same as ai_extract_uncertain_i64 but value is f64. |
| `ai_extract_uncertain_i64(prompt: str) -> Result<Uncertain<i64>, str>` | Send `prompt` to Anthropic with a structured-output tool. The LLM returns its answer plus a self-reported confidence in [0,1]. Returns Ok(Uncertain<i64>) or Err(reason). Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. |
| `append_file(path: str, content: str) -> Result<(), str>` | Append `content` to the end of `path`, creating the file if it does not exist. Returns Ok(()) or Err(message). This is the counterpart to `write_file`, which TRUNCATES — reaching for `write_file` twice to build a file up is the mistake this exists to prevent. Capability-wise it is a WRITE (`fs: [write(...)]`): it reads the existing bytes only in order to rewrite them and never surfaces them to the caller, so it opens no read channel. |
| `arr_all(xs: [T], pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> bool` | True if ALL elements satisfy the predicate. Short-circuits on first false. Empty array → true (vacuous truth). |
| `arr_any(xs: [T], pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> bool` | True if at least one element satisfies the predicate. Short-circuits. |
| `arr_argmax_f64(xs: [f64]) -> i64` | Index of the largest element in an f64 (or i64-coerced) array. |
| `arr_argmax_i64(xs: [i64]) -> i64` | Index of the largest element in an i64 array; ties broken by lowest index. Panics on empty. |
| `arr_argmin_f64(xs: [f64]) -> i64` | Index of the smallest element in an f64 (or i64-coerced) array. |
| `arr_argmin_i64(xs: [i64]) -> i64` | Index of the smallest element in an i64 array. |
| `arr_chunk(xs: [T], n: i64) -> [[T]]` | Split into consecutive chunks of size `n`; last chunk may be shorter. Panics on `n <= 0`. Useful for batched processing — pair with `arr_map` over the outer array. |
| `arr_concat(xs: [T], ys: [T]) -> [T]` | Concatenate two arrays into a fresh one (`xs ++ ys`); preserves order. Element runtime types must agree — no coercion. |
| `arr_contains(xs: [T], v: T) -> bool` | Linear scan: does `xs` contain a value structurally equal to `v`? Works for any element type — primitives, strings, tuples, nested arrays. |
| `arr_count_if(xs: [T], pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> i64` | Count elements where the predicate returns true. Equivalent to `len(arr_filter(xs, pred))` but doesn't materialize the filtered array. |
| `arr_drop(xs: [T], n: i64) -> [T]` | Return `xs` with the first `n` elements skipped. Saturates at `len(xs)`; negative `n` returns the full input. |
| `arr_drop_while(xs: [T], pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> [T]` | Skip leading elements satisfying `pred`, keep the rest. Complement of `arr_take_while`. |
| `arr_enumerate(xs: [T]) -> [(i64, T)]` | Pair each element with its index. `[a, b, c]` → `[(0,a), (1,b), (2,c)]`. The natural primitive for the iterate-with-index pattern. |
| `arr_filter(xs: [T], pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> [T]` | Keep elements where the predicate returns true. Element type is deferred — `arr_filter(["a", "bb"], \|s\| len(s) > 1)` works. Predicate that returns non-bool panics. |
| `arr_find(xs: [T], pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> Option<T>` | First element matching the predicate closure. Returns `Some(v)` or `None`. Same closure shape as `arr_filter` but returns a single element with early exit. |
| `arr_flatten(xss: [[T]]) -> [T]` | Flatten `[[T]]` to `[T]`. Each inner element must itself be an array. Useful after `arr_map` produces nested results. |
| `arr_fold(xs: [T], init: U, f: fn(U, T) -> U) -> U` | Reduce `xs` to a single value via `f(acc, x) -> acc`, threading `init` as the starting accumulator. Element type `T` and accumulator type `U` are both deferred, so `arr_fold([1, 2, 3], 0.0, \|a, x\| a + i64_to_f64(x))` works — most general combinator: sum, max, count, product are all special cases. |
| `arr_group_by(xs: [T], key_fn: fn(T) -> str) -> Dict` | Bucket `xs` by a closure that maps each element to a string key. Returns `Dict[str, [T]]`; elements appear in input order within each bucket. The natural "frequency table" / "by-category" reduction. |
| `arr_index_of(xs: [T], v: T) -> Option<i64>` | First index where the element structurally equals `v`. `Some(i)` if found, `None` otherwise. Pairs with `arr_contains` for the `where` follow-up to the `whether` question. |
| `arr_map(xs: [T], f: fn(T) -> U) -> [U]` | Apply a closure to each element, producing a fresh array of results. Element and result types are deferred — `arr_map([1, 2], \|x\| i64_to_str(x))` works. Closure panics propagate. |
| `arr_max_by(xs: [T], key_fn: fn(T) -> f64) -> T` | Element of `xs` that maximizes the numeric key fn. Folds map+argmax+index into one. Panics on empty. |
| `arr_max_f64(xs: [f64]) -> f64` | Maximum of an f64 array. Accepts i64 elements via coercion. Panics on empty. |
| `arr_max_i64(xs: [i64]) -> i64` | Maximum of an i64 array. Panics on an empty array — caller should guard with `if len(xs) > 0` first. |
| `arr_mean_f64(xs: [f64]) -> f64` | Arithmetic mean of an f64 (or i64-coerced) array. Empty → 0.0. |
| `arr_mean_i64(xs: [i64]) -> f64` | Arithmetic mean of an i64 array as f64. Empty → 0.0 (no NaN). |
| `arr_min_by(xs: [T], key_fn: fn(T) -> f64) -> T` | Element of `xs` that minimizes the numeric key fn. |
| `arr_min_f64(xs: [f64]) -> f64` | Minimum of an f64 array. Accepts i64 elements via coercion. Panics on empty. |
| `arr_min_i64(xs: [i64]) -> i64` | Minimum of an i64 array. Panics on an empty array. |
| `arr_partition(xs: [T], pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> ([T], [T])` | Split into `(yes, no)` tuple — elements satisfying `pred` and the rest. One pass over the input; complement of `arr_filter`. |
| `arr_push(xs: [T], x: T) -> [T]` | Return a fresh array with `x` appended. Copy semantics — the input is unaffected. Element type is deferred, so `arr_push(rows, Rec { .. })` builds a `[Rec]`; `T` must be consistent between the array and the pushed element (a mixed push is E0306). Native codegen lowers the `[i64]` case only — other element types are E0910-refused (interpreter-only). |
| `arr_range(start: i64, end: i64) -> [i64]` | Return the half-open range `[start, end)` as a fresh i64 slice. Empty when `end <= start`. Useful for `for i in arr_range(0, n)` and as a seed for further array ops. |
| `arr_repeat(v: T, n: i64) -> [T]` | Build an array of `n` copies of `v`. Useful to initialize a default-filled array before in-place mutation. Negative `n` returns empty; saturating cap at ~1M elements. |
| `arr_reverse(xs: [T]) -> [T]` | Return a fresh array with elements in reverse order. Works for any element type. |
| `arr_sort_by(xs: [T], cmp: fn(T, T) -> i64) -> [T]` | Return a sorted copy of `xs` using the comparator (neg = a<b, 0 = eq, pos = a>b). Element type is deferred so any sortable domain works. Stable insertion sort; closure-dispatch dominates cost on ASI-scale arrays. Input untouched. |
| `arr_std_f64(xs: [f64]) -> f64` | Sample standard deviation: sqrt of (sum of squared deviations from mean) / (n - 1). Panics for arrays of length < 2. |
| `arr_sum_by(xs: [T], key_fn: fn(T) -> i64) -> i64` | Sum a projected i64 field over `xs`. Equivalent to `arr_sum_i64(&arr_map(xs, key_fn))` but doesn't materialize the mapped array — the `_by` sibling of `arr_max_by`/`arr_min_by`. |
| `arr_sum_by_f64(xs: [T], key_fn: fn(T) -> f64) -> f64` | Sum a projected f64 field over `xs`. The f64 counterpart of `arr_sum_by`. |
| `arr_sum_f64(xs: [f64]) -> f64` | Sum of an f64 (or i64-coerced) array. Empty → 0.0. |
| `arr_sum_i64(xs: [i64]) -> i64` | Sum of an i64 array. Empty → 0. Saturates on overflow. |
| `arr_take(xs: [T], n: i64) -> [T]` | Return the first `n` elements of `xs`. Saturates at `len(xs)`; negative `n` returns empty. |
| `arr_take_while(xs: [T], pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> [T]` | Prefix of `xs` whose elements satisfy `pred`, up to (not including) the first failing element. The streaming-prefix dual of `arr_filter`. |
| `arr_unique(xs: [T]) -> [T]` | Dedupe preserving first occurrence and original order. Structural equality so nested values dedupe correctly. O(n²); hash-based version waits on a HashMap primitive. |
| `arr_zip(xs: [T], ys: [U]) -> [(T, U)]` | Pair two arrays element-wise into a slice of `(x, y)` tuples; truncates to the shorter input. Element types are deferred — works for any pair of arrays. Composes with `arr_map` / `arr_filter` for dataset zipping (features + labels). |
| `arr_zip_with(xs: [T], ys: [U], f: fn(T, U) -> V) -> [V]` | Pair element-wise then map via `f(x, y) -> z`. Truncates to the shorter input. More efficient than `arr_zip` + `arr_map` (no intermediate tuple slice) and the closure sees both values directly. |
| `as_f64(v: T) -> f64` | Numeric cast to f64. Accepts i64, f64, or bool; other types panic. Polymorphic on the source so call sites don't need to know the runtime type. Pairs with `as_i64` and supplants per-type `i64_to_f64` calls. |
| `as_i16(v: T) -> i16` | Numeric cast to i16 (truncating/masking, no panic). Accepts i64/f64/bool/any fixed-width int. Powers the `x as i16` operator. |
| `as_i32(v: T) -> i32` | Numeric cast to i32 (truncating/masking, no panic). Accepts i64/f64/bool/any fixed-width int. Powers the `x as i32` operator. |
| `as_i64(v: T) -> i64` | Numeric cast to i64. Accepts i64 (identity), f64 (truncating), or bool (0/1); other types panic. |
| `as_i8(v: T) -> i8` | Numeric cast to i8 (truncating/masking, no panic). Accepts i64/f64/bool/any fixed-width int. Powers the `x as i8` operator. |
| `as_u16(v: T) -> u16` | Numeric cast to u16 (truncating/masking, no panic). Accepts i64/f64/bool/any fixed-width int. Powers the `x as u16` operator. |
| `as_u32(v: T) -> u32` | Numeric cast to u32 (truncating/masking, no panic). Accepts i64/f64/bool/any fixed-width int. Powers the `x as u32` operator. |
| `as_u64(v: T) -> u64` | Numeric cast to u64 (bit-reinterpreting, no panic). Accepts i64/f64/bool/any fixed-width int. Powers the `x as u64` operator. |
| `as_u8(v: T) -> u8` | Numeric cast to u8 (truncating/masking, no panic). Accepts i64/f64/bool/any fixed-width int. Powers the `x as u8` operator. |
| `assert(cond: bool) -> ()` | Panic with a diagnostic message if `cond` is false. |
| `assert_eq(a: i64, b: i64) -> ()` | Panic if `a != b`. Compares two i64 values. |
| `assert_eq_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> ()` | Panic if `a != b`. Compares two f64 values. |
| `assert_eq_str(a: str, b: str) -> ()` | Panic with a diff if `a != b`. Compares two str values. |
| `assert_err(tag: bool) -> ()` | Panic if `tag` is true (Ok). Expects the i1 tag from a Result. |
| `atomic_cas_i64(ptr: i64, expected: i64, desired: i64, ordering: i64) -> i64` | R17 Slice 2: atomic compare-and-swap — if `*ptr == expected`, store `desired`; returns the value that WAS in memory (== expected iff the swap happened) with the named memory order. Lowers to LLVM `cmpxchg`. Substrate-only. |
| `atomic_fetch_add_i64(ptr: i64, delta: i64, ordering: i64) -> i64` | R17 Slice 2: atomically add `delta` to `*ptr`, returning the PRIOR value, with the named memory order. Lowers to LLVM `atomicrmw add`. The race-free SMP counter primitive. Substrate-only. |
| `atomic_load_i64(ptr: i64, ordering: i64) -> i64` | R17 Slice 2: atomic load of an i64 from `ptr` with the named memory order (0=relaxed,1=acquire,2=release,3=acq_rel,4=seq_cst). Lowers to LLVM `load atomic`. Substrate-only. |
| `atomic_store_i64(ptr: i64, val: i64, ordering: i64) -> ()` | R17 Slice 2: atomic store of `val` to `ptr` with the named memory order. Lowers to LLVM `store atomic`. Substrate-only. |
| `axon_concat(a: str, b: str) -> str` | Concatenate two strings; used internally by string interpolation. |
| `base64_decode(s: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Decode standard base64. Err (E2204) on invalid characters, bad padding, OR when the decoded bytes are not valid UTF-8 — Axon has no bytes type and `str` must be valid UTF-8, so this round-trips TEXT only. That limitation is stated rather than papered over: returning replacement characters or a truncated prefix would be a silently lossy decode, which is the class of bug this spec exists to remove. |
| `base64_encode(s: str) -> str` | Standard base64 (RFC 4648 alphabet, `=` padded) of `s`'s UTF-8 bytes. |
| `beta_cdf(alpha: f64, beta_b: f64, x: f64) -> f64` | Phase 13: Beta cumulative distribution P(X ≤ x) for X ~ Beta(alpha, beta_b). Uses regularized incomplete beta (Lentz continued-fraction). Panics if alpha ≤ 0 or beta_b ≤ 0. Returns 0 for x ≤ 0, 1 for x ≥ 1. Pure. |
| `beta_mean(alpha: f64, beta_b: f64) -> f64` | Phase 13: Expected value of Beta(alpha, beta_b) = alpha / (alpha + beta_b). Panics if alpha ≤ 0 or beta_b ≤ 0. Pure. |
| `beta_sample(alpha: f64, beta_b: f64) -> f64` | Phase 13: Sample from Beta(alpha, beta_b) via Gamma ratio (Marsaglia-Tsang). Returns value in [0, 1]. Panics if alpha ≤ 0 or beta_b ≤ 0. Impure: Random effect. |
| `beta_variance(alpha: f64, beta_b: f64) -> f64` | Phase 13: Variance of Beta(alpha, beta_b) = alpha*beta_b / ((alpha+beta_b)²*(alpha+beta_b+1)). Panics if alpha ≤ 0 or beta_b ≤ 0. Pure. |
| `bit_and(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Bitwise AND of two i64 values (`a & b`). |
| `bit_not(n: i64) -> i64` | Bitwise NOT (complement) of an i64 value (`~n`). |
| `bit_or(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Bitwise OR of two i64 values (`a \| b`). |
| `bit_xor(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Bitwise XOR of two i64 values (`a ^ b`). |
| `bpf_get_smp_processor_id() -> i64` | R23 eBPF: the current CPU id. Lowers to BPF `call 8`. Substrate-only. |
| `bpf_ktime_get_ns() -> i64` | R23 eBPF: nanoseconds since boot (CLOCK_MONOTONIC). Lowers to BPF `call 5`. Substrate-only. |
| `bpf_map_lookup_elem(map: i64, key: i64) -> i64` | R23 eBPF: look up `key` in BPF map handle `map` (Slice 1: handle 0 = the single ARRAY map). Returns the value pointer as i64 (0 = miss). Lowers to BPF `call 1`. Substrate-only. |
| `bpf_map_value_add(value_ptr: i64, delta: i64) -> ()` | R23 eBPF: atomically add `delta` to the i64 a map value pointer refers to (the race-free counter increment). Lowers to BPF `atomicrmw add`. Substrate-only. |
| `categorical_cdf(probs: [f64], k: i64) -> f64` | Phase 13: Categorical cumulative distribution P(X ≤ k) = sum(probs[0..=k]). Returns 0 for k < 0, 1 for k ≥ len(probs). Panics on empty probs. Pure. |
| `categorical_mean(probs: [f64]) -> f64` | Phase 13: Expected value of Categorical(probs) treating indices as values: sum(i * probs[i]). Panics on empty probs. Pure. |
| `categorical_sample(probs: [f64]) -> i64` | Phase 13: Sample from Categorical(probs) — returns index i with probability probs[i]. Panics on empty probs. Impure: Random effect. |
| `categorical_variance(probs: [f64]) -> f64` | Phase 13: Variance of Categorical(probs): E[X²] - E[X]². Panics on empty probs. Pure. |
| `ceil(n: f64) -> f64` | Smallest integer not less than `n`. Calls C ceil. |
| `ceil_f64(x: f64) -> f64` | Round `x` up to the nearest integer (as `f64`). |
| `char_at(s: str, i: i64) -> i64` | Return the byte value (0-255) of `s` at byte index `i`, or -1 if `i` is out of range. |
| `char_code(c: str) -> Result<i64, str>` | The Unicode code point of a ONE-character string. `Err` if `c` is empty or holds more than one character. The inverse of `chr`, which goes code point -> string; `chr` PANICS on an invalid code point where this returns `Err`, an asymmetry kept deliberately rather than changing `chr`'s shipped signature. |
| `char_is_alpha(c: str) -> bool` | True when `c` is exactly one character and that character is alphabetic (Unicode-aware, so `é` counts). False for the empty string and for multi-character input. |
| `char_is_digit(c: str) -> bool` | True when `c` is exactly one character and that character is an ASCII digit 0-9. False for the empty string, for multi-character input, and for non-ASCII digits — so it is a predicate about ASCII digits, not about Unicode numeric-ness. |
| `char_is_space(c: str) -> bool` | True when `c` is exactly one character and that character is whitespace (Unicode-aware). False for the empty string and for multi-character input. |
| `chr(n: i64) -> str` | Return a one-character string for the given Unicode code point. Panics if n is not a valid code point (0–0x10FFFF). |
| `clamp_f64(n: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64` | Clamp `n` to the range `[lo, hi]`. |
| `clamp_i64(n: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64` | Clamp `n` to the range `[lo, hi]`. |
| `cli() -> ()` | R17 HAL: execute the x86_64 `cli` instruction — clear interrupt flag (disable interrupts). Substrate-only. |
| `corrigible_halt() -> ()` | Trip the corrigibility kill-switch (R9). After this, every call to an `@[corrigible]` function is REFUSED — its body never runs — and the latch never clears. There is deliberately no resume: a reversible kill-switch is not a kill-switch. A refused call exits the program with code 4 (distinct from panic/verify/static) so a supervisor can detect that the switch fired. The system cannot resist or reverse its own shutdown. |
| `corrigible_halted() -> bool` | Report whether the corrigibility kill-switch (R9) is latched. `true` once `corrigible_halt()` has been called, forever after. Lets a program or supervisor branch on the shutdown state without triggering a refusal. |
| `decimal_abs(d: Decimal) -> Decimal` | Absolute value of a `Decimal`. Overflow (at the i128 minimum) is a graceful panic, never a wrap. |
| `decimal_div(a: Decimal, b: Decimal, mode: str) -> Decimal` | Divide `a / b` to scale 9 with an EXPLICIT rounding `mode` (money division must specify rounding). Division by zero is a graceful panic. The `/` operator uses the half_even default; this builtin lets you pick the mode. |
| `decimal_from_str(s: str) -> Result<Decimal,str>` | Parse `s` (e.g. "1.50", "-0.25", "100") into an exact fixed-point `Decimal` at scale 9. `Err(str)` on malformed input or excess precision (>9 fractional digits). The input-side inverse of `decimal_to_str` — round-trips exactly. |
| `decimal_neg(d: Decimal) -> Decimal` | Negate a `Decimal`. Overflow (at the i128 minimum) is a graceful panic. |
| `decimal_round(d: Decimal, dp: i64, mode: str) -> Decimal` | Round `d` to `dp` fractional digits (0–9) using rounding `mode` ("half_even" [banker's], "half_up", "down", "up"). The result stays at scale 9. Unknown mode or dp>9 is a graceful panic. |
| `decimal_to_str(d: Decimal) -> str` | Render a `Decimal` to its canonical exact string (trailing zeros stripped; whole numbers print with no point). Exact inverse of `decimal_from_str`. |
| `dict_each(d: Dict, f: fn(str, V)) -> ()` | Iterate (k, v) pairs for side effects. The closure's return is ignored. Use this when you don't need a new dict — pair with println, write_file, etc. |
| `dict_filter(d: Dict, pred: fn(str, V) -> bool) -> Dict` | Keep entries where the predicate `(key, value) -> bool` holds. Returns a fresh dict. The dict analogue of `arr_filter`; closure sees both key and value. |
| `dict_from_pairs(xs: [(str, V)]) -> Dict` | Build a Dict from a slice of `(str, V)` tuples. Duplicate keys: last pair wins. |
| `dict_from_str(s: str) -> Dict` | Parse a `dict_to_str` payload back into a Dict (lenient). Values come back as `str`; caller converts via `parse_int` / `parse_float` if numeric. Empty AND malformed lines (no `=`) are skipped — never panics. Use `dict_try_from_str` to reject malformed input as a `Result` instead. Inverse of `dict_to_str`. |
| `dict_get(d: Dict, k: str) -> Option<T>` | Return `Some(v)` if key `k` is present in `d`, `None` otherwise. Value type is deferred. |
| `dict_get_or(d: Dict, k: str, default: V) -> V` | Get the value at `k` or return `default` if absent. Compresses the `match dict_get(d, k) { Some(v) => v  None => default }` idiom into one call. |
| `dict_has(d: Dict, k: str) -> bool` | Does `d` contain key `k`? |
| `dict_inc(d: Dict, k: str) -> i64` | Atomically bump an i64 counter at `k`. Initializes to 1 if absent. Returns the new value. Replaces the four-line get-default-add-set dance for frequency / counter tables. |
| `dict_keys(d: Dict) -> [str]` | All keys in `d`, in BTreeMap (lexicographic) order. Deterministic. |
| `dict_len(d: Dict) -> i64` | Number of entries in `d`. |
| `dict_map_values(d: Dict, f: fn(V) -> U) -> Dict` | Transform every value via the closure; keys preserved. Returns a fresh dict — the input is not mutated. The dict analogue of `arr_map`. |
| `dict_merge(d1: Dict, d2: Dict) -> Dict` | Union of two dicts; right-biased on key collision (values in `d2` win). Returns a fresh dict — inputs are unchanged. |
| `dict_new() -> Dict` | Fresh empty string-keyed map. Reference-shared like Chan: mutating builtins update the same underlying state every handle sees. |
| `dict_remove(d: Dict, k: str) -> Option<T>` | Remove the entry for `k` from `d`; return the prior value as `Some(v)` if present, `None` otherwise. |
| `dict_set(d: Dict, k: str, v: T) -> ()` | Set `d[k] = v` (overwriting any prior value). Mutates `d` in place via its shared RefCell. |
| `dict_to_json(d: Dict) -> Result<str, str>` | Serialize a whole Dict to a JSON object. `Err` if any value has no JSON form (a closure, a channel). Distinct from `dict_to_str`, which emits Axon's own dict rendering rather than JSON. |
| `dict_to_pairs(d: Dict) -> [(str, V)]` | Entries as a slice of `(str, V)` tuples in BTreeMap key order. The natural primitive for "sort a dict by value": `dict_to_pairs → arr_sort_by → arr_take`. |
| `dict_to_str(d: Dict) -> Result<str, str>` | Serialize a dict to a line-oriented `key=value\n` format. Returns `Err(msg)` when a key contains `=`/`\n` or a value contains `\n` (the format can't represent them) — recoverable, never a host panic. Values are rendered via `display` (numeric values stringify). Deterministic — BTreeMap key order. `Ok(s)` round-trips through `dict_from_str`. |
| `dict_try_from_str(s: str) -> Result<Dict, str>` | Strict `dict_from_str` (BUG_HUNT #31): parse a `dict_to_str` payload, returning `Err(message)` on the first malformed line (no `=`) instead of skipping it. The Result-returning form for parsing untrusted input — a malformed line is recoverable, not a crash. |
| `dict_values(d: Dict) -> [T]` | All values in `d`, in key-sorted order. |
| `dir_create(path: str) -> Result<(), str>` | Create `path`, including any missing parent directories (like `mkdir -p`). Ok(()) if it already exists. |
| `dir_list(path: str) -> Result<[str], str>` | Entry NAMES (not full paths) directly inside `path`, sorted, non-recursive. Sorted because `read_dir` order is filesystem-dependent and a program whose output varies run-to-run breaks replay. Capability-wise a READ, and strictly more leakage than reading a file: it discloses names the caller did not already know. |
| `dstore_apply(handle: i64, op_id: i64, delta: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 4): apply op `op_id` with effect `delta`; returns the new value. Under linearizable a retried op_id is deduped (exactly-once, even across a process restart); under at_least_once it re-applies. An applied op is appended to the durable log. |
| `dstore_clear(key: str) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 4): delete a durable store's log (reset persistence). Returns 1 if a log existed and was removed, else 0. |
| `dstore_open(key: str, consistency: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 4): open (and replay the durable log of) the store `key` with a consistency model (0=at_least_once, 1=linearizable). Returns its handle. The replayed state survives a fresh process. |
| `dstore_value(handle: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 4): the store's current accumulated value. |
| `dstore_version(handle: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 4): the monotonic total-order stamp (counts distinct applied ops under linearizable; stays 0 under at_least_once). |
| `env_var(name: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Read the environment variable `name`. Returns Ok(value) or Err("not set"). |
| `eprint(msg: str) -> ()` | Write `msg` to stderr without a trailing newline. |
| `eprintln(msg: str) -> ()` | Write `msg` to stderr followed by a newline. |
| `exec(cmd: str, args: [str]) -> Result<str, str>` | Spawn a process: run `cmd` with `args`, returning Ok(stdout) on success or Err(message) on failure. Exercises the `exec` capability — a `@[contained(exec: none)]` fn that calls this is rejected at compile time (E1001), and `never: [exec]` hard-denies it. The active host may refuse exec entirely (a sandboxed/browser host returns Err). Use for shelling out to external tools from a trusted zone. |
| `exit(code: i64) -> ()` | Terminate the process immediately with the given exit code. |
| `exp(x: f64) -> f64` | Natural exponential e^x. Useful for sigmoids, softmax, decay functions. |
| `f64_to_i64(x: f64) -> i64` | Truncate an `f64` to `i64` (rounds toward zero). |
| `file_copy(from: str, to: str) -> Result<(), str>` | Copy `from` to `to`, truncating the destination. The ONLY builtin needing two different capabilities on two different arguments: arg 0 is a READ and arg 1 is a WRITE. A checker that granted it on the write capability alone would let a write-only `@[contained]` fn exfiltrate a read-denied file to a path it controls, which is why capability classification is per-argument. |
| `file_exists(path: str) -> bool` | True when `path` exists. Capability-wise this is a READ (`fs: [read(...)]`), not a free query: probing existence is an information channel — it discloses whether a path exists without reading it, which is exactly what a sandbox's read allowlist is for. |
| `file_rename(from: str, to: str) -> Result<(), str>` | Rename or move `from` to `to`. BOTH paths are WRITES — the source is destroyed, so a read capability on it is not enough. |
| `file_size(path: str) -> Result<i64, str>` | The size of `path` in BYTES (not characters — a multi-byte UTF-8 character counts once per byte). Returns Ok(n), or Err(message) if the file cannot be read. Note this READS the file to measure it, so it costs O(size) and requires valid UTF-8: it is not a `stat`, and a binary file reports an error rather than a size. |
| `floor(n: f64) -> f64` | Largest integer not greater than `n`. Calls C floor. |
| `floor_f64(x: f64) -> f64` | Round `x` down to the nearest integer (as `f64`). |
| `fn_addr(name: str) -> i64` | R17: the address of the function named `name`, as a raw i64. `name` MUST be a compile-time string literal naming a fn defined in this program — E1707 if it is not a literal, or names no known function. Used to fill hardware descriptor-table entries (e.g. an IDT gate's offset fields) that must point at an @[interrupt] handler. Substrate-only; codegen-only (E0910 in interp — a function's address is meaningless in a tree-walking interpreter). |
| `format(template: str) -> str` | Interpolate `template` and return the resulting string. |
| `gaussian_cdf(mu: f64, sigma: f64, x: f64) -> f64` | Phase 13: Gaussian cumulative distribution P(X ≤ x) for X ~ N(mu, sigma²). Uses erf approximation (max error ≤ 1.5e-7). Panics if sigma ≤ 0. Pure. |
| `gaussian_pdf(mu: f64, sigma: f64, x: f64) -> f64` | Phase 13: Gaussian probability density function at `x` for N(mu, sigma²). Panics if sigma ≤ 0. Pure. |
| `gaussian_sample(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> f64` | Phase 13: Sample from N(mu, sigma²) using Box-Muller transform. Panics if sigma ≤ 0. Impure: Random effect. |
| `goal_best_input(name: str, target: f64) -> i64` | Return the leading-i64 input that produced the best observed score (closest to `target`) for the @[adaptive] function `name`. Pairs with `goal_run` so an ASI loop can introspect which probe got it there. For multi-arg adaptive fns this returns the FIRST dim; use `goal_best_inputs` for the full tuple. Returns 0 when no inputs were recorded. |
| `goal_best_inputs(name: str, target: f64) -> [i64]` | Return all i64 input dims that produced the best observed score for the @[adaptive] function `name`. The multi-arg companion to `goal_best_input` — for `fn(x: i64, y: i64) -> i64` it returns `[x*, y*]`. Empty slice when the fn was never called. |
| `goal_best_inputs_f64(name: str, target: f64) -> [f64]` | Return all f64 input dims that produced the best observed score for an `@[adaptive] fn(f64, …) -> f64`. The continuous-domain companion to `goal_best_inputs`: pairs with the f64 hill-climb path for linear-regression weights, control parameters, and other real-valued search problems. |
| `goal_best_score(name: str, target: f64) -> f64` | Best observed score for an @[adaptive] fn, read from the in-memory provenance store without running any new optimization. Equivalent to `goal_run(name, target, 0)` but does NOT mutate state — pure query. Returns `target` when no records exist. |
| `goal_clear(name: str) -> i64` | Drop the recorded provenance for the @[adaptive] function `name` so a follow-up `goal_run` starts fresh. Returns the count of evicted records. |
| `goal_continue(name: str, target: f64, max_evals: i64) -> f64` | Warm-start variant of `goal_run`: seeds the optimizer at the best prior probe from in-memory provenance rather than the origin. Pair with `goal_run` for iterative refinement — each `goal_continue` call resumes where the last left off. Falls through to a fresh run when no prior best exists, so calling cold is a no-op. |
| `goal_count(name: str) -> i64` | Number of provenance entries recorded for an @[adaptive] fn. Equivalent to `len(goal_history(name))` but O(1) — avoids materializing the trace just to count it. Returns 0 if the fn has no recorded calls. |
| `goal_eval(name: str, input: i64) -> f64` | HELD-OUT evaluation (R5): run the @[adaptive] metric `name` on a specific `input` and return its score WITHOUT recording it as a training probe (provenance is snapshotted+restored). The eval-hierarchy primitive — optimize with `goal_run` on a training budget, then `goal_eval` the best input on a held-out test set to check the target honestly (no overfitting to probes, no bias to the next goal_run). |
| `goal_history(name: str) -> [(i64, f64)]` | Return the full optimization trace as a slice of `(input, score)` tuples, in call order, for the @[adaptive] function `name`. Empty when nothing was recorded. |
| `goal_run(name: str, target: f64, max_evals: i64) -> f64` | Optimize the @[adaptive] function `name` toward `target` for up to `max_evals` evaluations, then return the best score across ALL accumulated provenance. **`max_evals <= 0` means UNLIMITED, not zero** (`hill_climb_i64`: `let unlimited = max_evals <= 0`) — measured, a fresh run with `max_evals: 0` performed 28 evaluations where `max_evals: 20` performed 12. So a CALLER PASSING A COMPUTED BUDGET MUST CLAMP IT: a budget that reaches 0 because it is exhausted triggers the LARGEST search, not none. Use `goal_best_input`/`goal_history` for a retrospective read that runs nothing — not just this call's probes. NOTE: because the result is cumulative, comparing two `goal_run` calls with different budgets (A/B testing a budget) will NOT show the budget's effect — the second call sees the first call's best too. To isolate a run, `goal_clear(name)` first. Errors if `name` is neither a defined fn nor previously recorded (typo guard). Returns `target` only when an empty provenance set somehow remains. |
| `goal_run_categorical(name: str, n_choices: i64, target: f64, max_evals: i64) -> f64` | Categorical (unordered-choice) search: optimize the @[adaptive] function `name` whose single i64 argument is a CHOICE INDEX in `[0, n_choices)`. Unlike `goal_run` (which hill-climbs and treats adjacent indices as near), this makes NO ordinal assumption — right for a set of unrelated options (prompt templates, models, strategies) where a gradient is meaningless. When the budget covers the whole set (`max_evals <= 0` or `n_choices <= max_evals`) it is EXHAUSTIVE — every choice evaluated, the true best guaranteed; otherwise it random-samples `max_evals` choices. Returns the best score (closest to `target`); provenance accumulates so `goal_best_input` reads the winning choice back. |
| `goal_run_constrained(name: str, constraint: str, target: f64, max_evals: i64) -> f64` | Constrained search (`subject_to`): optimize the @[adaptive] function `name` toward `target` like `goal_run`, but only over candidates the boolean `constraint` function ACCEPTS. `constraint` names a fn sharing `name`'s parameter list and returning `bool`; an infeasible candidate is scored maximally-distant so the optimizer rejects it — a HARD feasibility gate, not a soft penalty folded into the metric. The constraint runs as a plain (non-@[adaptive]) call, so it never pollutes the score trajectory. Errors if `constraint` is not a defined fn. If every candidate is infeasible the result is a far-from-target sentinel (no feasible solution found). |
| `goal_run_multistart(name: str, target: f64, n_starts: i64, evals_per_start: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> f64` | Multi-start hill-climb strategy: pick `n_starts` random starting points in `[lo, hi)` (per-dim) and run coordinate-descent hill-climb (with Powell joint step) from each with `evals_per_start` budget. Returns the best score across all starts. Standard recipe for escaping local optima while preserving gradient-style refinement once a basin is found. |
| `goal_run_random(name: str, target: f64, n_samples: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> f64` | Random-search strategy: sample `n_samples` random i64 tuples uniformly in `[lo, hi)` (per-dim independent) and score each via the @[adaptive] function `name`. Returns the best observed score. Baseline against `goal_run`'s hill climb — useful for multi-modal objectives or sanity-checking that the optimizer is actually doing something. Provenance accumulates as a side effect. |
| `hex_decode(s: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Decode lowercase or uppercase hex. Err (E2204) on an odd length, a non-hex digit, or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 — same text-only limitation as `base64_decode`. |
| `hex_encode(s: str) -> str` | Lowercase hex of `s`'s UTF-8 bytes. |
| `hlt() -> ()` | R17 HAL: execute the x86_64 `hlt` instruction — halts the CPU until the next interrupt. Used in the idle loop of a freestanding kernel. Substrate-only. |
| `host_await(req: str) -> str` | Suspend, yield `req` to the host, resume with its reply (str). Needs a suspendable host (R15). |
| `host_await_opt(req: str) -> Option<str>` | Suspend, yield `req`, resume with `Some(reply)` or `None` at end-of-input (R15). |
| `host_await_val(req: T) -> U` | Suspend, yield any-typed `req` to the host, resume with its (any-typed) reply. Dict/struct/enum payloads cross via a Send deep-clone; a Chan payload is refused (R15 Slice 2). |
| `host_await_val_opt(req: T) -> Option<U>` | Suspend, yield any-typed `req`, resume with `Some(reply)` or `None` at end-of-input. Dict/struct payloads cross via a Send deep-clone (R15 Slice 2). |
| `http_get(url: str, headers: str) -> Result<str, str>` | HTTP GET `url` with `headers` (a JSON object string, pass `""` for no custom headers). Returns Ok(body) on a 2xx response or Err("HTTP <status>: <body>") on failure. Carries the `Net` effect row. Requires the `asi-runtime` Cargo feature. |
| `http_post(url: str, headers: str, body: str) -> Result<str, str>` | HTTP POST `url` with `headers` (JSON object string) and `body`. Returns Ok(response_body) on 2xx or Err("HTTP <status>: <body>") on failure. Carries the `Net` effect row. |
| `http_sse(url: str, headers: str, on_event: fn(str) -> ()) -> Result<i64, str>` | Stream Server-Sent Events from `url` via GET. Sets `Accept: text/event-stream` automatically. `headers` is a JSON object string (pass `""` for none). `on_event` is called once per SSE event with the `data:` payload. Returns Ok(event_count) or Err(message). Carries the `Net` effect row. Requires the `asi-runtime` Cargo feature. |
| `http_sse_post(url: str, headers: str, body: str, on_event: fn(str) -> ()) -> Result<i64, str>` | Stream Server-Sent Events from `url` via POST (required by LLM provider APIs). Sets `Accept: text/event-stream` automatically. `headers` is a JSON object string; `body` is the POST body (typically JSON). `on_event` is called once per SSE event. Returns Ok(event_count) or Err(message). Carries the `Net` effect row. Requires the `asi-runtime` Cargo feature. |
| `i64_to_f64(n: i64) -> f64` | Convert an `i64` to the nearest `f64`. |
| `i64_to_str_radix(n: i64, base: i64) -> str` | Convert `n` to a string in the given base (2–36). Negative numbers are prefixed with '-'. Bases outside 2–36 return an empty string. |
| `json_arr_f64(json: str) -> Result<[f64], str>` | A whole JSON array of numbers as `[f64]`, parsing once. Integer elements widen. |
| `json_arr_from_f64(xs: [f64]) -> str` | Build a JSON array from `[f64]`. Non-finite values (NaN, infinity) have no JSON representation and are emitted as `null`, matching what every mainstream JSON encoder does. |
| `json_arr_from_i64(xs: [i64]) -> str` | Build a JSON array from `[i64]`. The inverse of `json_arr_i64`. |
| `json_arr_from_str(xs: [str]) -> str` | Build a JSON array from `[str]`, escaping each element. The inverse of `json_arr_str`. |
| `json_arr_i64(json: str) -> Result<[i64], str>` | A whole JSON array of integers as `[i64]`, parsing the document ONCE. The idiom for summing or folding a JSON array; Err (E2202) if any element is not an integer. |
| `json_arr_str(json: str) -> Result<[str], str>` | A whole JSON array of strings as `[str]`, parsing once. Err (E2202) if any element is not a string. |
| `json_at(json: str, i: i64) -> Result<str, str>` | The `i`-th element of a JSON array, returned AS A JSON STRING so it composes with every other json_* function. For a homogeneous array of numbers prefer `json_arr_i64`, which parses once: `json_at` in a loop re-parses the whole document per call and is therefore O(n^2) over the array. |
| `json_from_pairs(pairs: [(str, str)]) -> str` | Build a JSON object from (key, PRE-ENCODED JSON value) pairs. Each value is inserted verbatim, so it must already be valid JSON — use `json_stringify` for a string, `to_str` for a number, `json_arr_from_i64` for an array. Keys ARE escaped for you. The counterpart to the json_* readers: Slice 3 made a document navigable, this makes one writable. |
| `json_get_i64(json: str, key: str) -> Result<i64, str>` | Extract an integer field from a JSON object string. Returns Ok(n) or Err(reason). |
| `json_get_json(json: str, key: str) -> Result<str, str>` | The value at top-level `key`, returned AS A JSON STRING — the accessor that makes sub-objects and sub-arrays reachable. `json_get_i64`/`json_get_str` only reach scalar fields. |
| `json_get_str(json: str, key: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Extract a string field from a JSON object string. Returns Ok(value) or Err(reason). |
| `json_keys(json: str) -> Result<[str], str>` | The keys of a JSON object, SORTED (not in document order — the parser backs objects with a BTreeMap, so the order is lexicographic and deterministic regardless of how the document was written). `Err` on an array or scalar. |
| `json_len(json: str) -> Result<i64, str>` | Number of elements in a JSON array, or number of keys in a JSON object. `Err` on a scalar or malformed input. Without this an array could be reached but not LOOPED, which is why summing `{"a": [1,2,3]}` was impossible before R42. |
| `json_parse(s: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Validate `s` as JSON. Returns Ok(s) if valid, Err(reason) if not. Pure; no network call. |
| `json_path_f64(json: str, path: str) -> Result<f64, str>` | The float at a dot-separated path. Accepts an integer leaf and widens it, since JSON does not distinguish 4 from 4.0. |
| `json_path_i64(json: str, path: str) -> Result<i64, str>` | The integer at a dot-separated path. `json_path_str` reaches only STRING leaves, so this is what a numeric leaf needed: `json_path_i64(doc, "b.c")`. Err (E2202) if the leaf is not an integer. |
| `json_path_json(json: str, path: str) -> Result<str, str>` | As `json_path_str`, but returning the sub-document at the dot-separated path's leaf AS A JSON STRING rather than only a string leaf. Numeric path components index arrays (`"a.1"`). The leaf is RE-SERIALISED, so an object comes back canonicalised (keys sorted, whitespace dropped), not as the original bytes. |
| `json_path_str(json: str, path: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Navigate a dot-separated path into a JSON object and return the string value at the leaf. E.g. `json_path_str(event, "delta.text")` navigates `event["delta"]["text"]`. Returns Ok(value) or Err(reason). |
| `json_stringify(s: str) -> str` | JSON-encode a string value: wraps in double quotes and escapes special characters. For numbers/booleans use to_str first. |
| `kernel_goal_best_score(goal: i64) -> f64` | Phase-7 (R12b): best observed score for a kernel goal (no new spend). |
| `kernel_goal_budget_left(goal: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12b): the goal's principal's remaining budget (no new spend). |
| `kernel_goal_create(principal: i64, name: str, target: f64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12b): register a goal optimizing the `@[adaptive]` fn `name` toward `target`, scoped to `principal` (its budget bounds total spend). Returns an opaque goal handle. Panics if `name` is neither a defined fn nor a recorded goal. |
| `kernel_goal_run(goal: i64, max_evals: i64) -> f64` | Phase-7 (R12b): run up to `max_evals` optimizer evaluations, but no more than the principal's remaining budget; debit that budget by the evals used and return the best score. If the budget bounds the run short of `max_evals`, the goal STOPS and the program exits 7 (E1604, goal budget exhausted) — the partial best stays queryable via kernel_goal_best_score. |
| `kernel_goal_spent(goal: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12b): number of evaluations charged to the principal for this goal. |
| `len(s: str) -> i64` | Return the number of bytes in `s`. |
| `lidt(idtr_addr: i64) -> ()` | R17 HAL: execute the x86_64 `lidt` instruction — loads the Interrupt Descriptor Table register from a 10-byte IDTR structure (2-byte limit, 8-byte base) at `idtr_addr`. The caller is responsible for constructing that structure (e.g. a `@[repr(C)] @[packed] { limit: u16, base: u64 }`) and obtaining its address — `lidt` itself only consumes the address, like `ptr_from_addr`/`volatile_load_*` do (see R17 spec §12 Q8 for the still-open "address of an Axon-owned value" gap this runs into in practice). Substrate-only. |
| `llm_alive(gw: i64) -> bool` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 5): has the gateway NOT yet latched on a budget overrun? |
| `llm_complete(gw: i64, prompt: str, tokens: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 5): mediate one AI call — charge the real token cost against the principal's budget when it fits (returns the µ$ charged); on overrun spend nothing, return -1, and LATCH the gateway (later calls also fall back). There is no un-metered path. |
| `llm_open(model: str, rate_micro: i64, principal: i64, fallback: str) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 5): open an LLM gateway scoped to a principal; rate_micro is µ$ per 1000 tokens. Every call's per-token cost is debited from the principal's budget. Returns the gateway handle; panics E1604 on an unknown principal. |
| `llm_spent(gw: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 5): µ$ spent through this gateway so far. |
| `ln(x: f64) -> f64` | Natural log of `x`. `x <= 0` returns NaN (matches Rust f64::ln). UCB-style algorithms use `ln(t)` where t ≥ 1, so this is fine in practice. |
| `log10(x: f64) -> f64` | Base-10 log of `x`. Use for human-readable scales (orders of magnitude). |
| `max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64` | Return the larger of two `f64` values. |
| `max_i32(a: i64, b: i64) -> i32` | Return the greater of two integers (truncated to i32 range). |
| `max_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Return the greater of two i64 values. |
| `min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64` | Return the smaller of two `f64` values. |
| `min_i32(a: i64, b: i64) -> i32` | Return the lesser of two integers (truncated to i32 range). |
| `min_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Return the lesser of two i64 values. |
| `now_ms() -> i64` | Return the current wall-clock time as milliseconds since the Unix epoch. |
| `parse_bool(s: str) -> Result<bool, str>` | Parse `"true"` or `"false"`. Returns `Ok(true/false)` or `Err("invalid bool")`. |
| `parse_bool_or(s: str, default: bool) -> bool` | Parse `s` as bool (`"true"` / `"false"`); fall back to `default` if neither. |
| `parse_float(s: str) -> Result<f64, str>` | Parse `s` as a 64-bit float. Returns Ok(n) or Err(message). |
| `parse_float_or(s: str, default: f64) -> f64` | Parse `s` as f64; fall back to `default` if malformed. |
| `parse_int(s: str) -> Result<i64,str>` | Parse `s` (surrounding whitespace trimmed) as a base-10 integer. Base-10 only — a radix prefix like `0x1F` returns `Err` with a hint to strip it. The `Err(str)` names the offending input. |
| `parse_int_or(s: str, default: i64) -> i64` | Parse `s` as i64; fall back to `default` if the string is missing or malformed. Folds the `Result`-match ceremony away — useful in load-from-disk paths where bad inputs should silently default rather than propagate. |
| `parse_int_radix(s: str, base: i64) -> Result<i64,str>` | Parse `s` (whitespace trimmed) as an integer in the given `base` (2–36); the radix-aware counterpart to `parse_int` (base 10) and the input-side inverse of `i64_to_str_radix`. A matching radix prefix is accepted and stripped (`0x`/`0X` for base 16, `0o`/`0O` for 8, `0b`/`0B` for 2); a leading `-` is allowed. `Err(str)` names the offending input on a bad digit; a `base` outside 2–36 is `Err`, never a panic. |
| `port_in_u8(port: i64) -> i64` | R17 HAL: read one byte from an x86 I/O port (`inb port` → zero-extended i64). Used for polling UART LSR, reading keyboard status, etc. Substrate-only. |
| `port_out_u8(port: i64, val: i64) -> ()` | R17 HAL: write one byte to an x86 I/O port (`outb val, port`). Used for PIC, serial UART, and debug console (port 0xE9 = QEMU debugcon). Substrate-only. |
| `pow(base: f64, exp: f64) -> f64` | Raise `base` to the power `exp`. Calls C pow. |
| `pow_i64(base: i64, exp: i64) -> i64` | Raise `base` to the power `exp` (non-negative `exp` only). |
| `principal_activate(handle: i64) -> ()` | F3 (Phase 9): set the named principal as the current audit context so capability audit records (ai_call, agent_action) carry its name. A negative or unknown handle is a PANIC (E1601), not a silent reset to "root" — audit attribution that fails open would let a bad handle launder a call back to the root authority. Interp-only. |
| `principal_authorize(handle: i64, needs_net: bool, needs_fs_write: bool, needs_exec: bool) -> bool` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 1): action gate — authorized iff the principal holds every needed capability AND is not budget-exhausted. |
| `principal_budget_remaining(handle: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 1): the principal's remaining budget (cap − used, clamped at 0). 0 for an unknown handle. |
| `principal_can_mint(handle: i64, want_net: bool, want_fs_write: bool, want_exec: bool, grant: i64) -> bool` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 1): would a mint grant anything — does the parent hold every requested cap and have budget to carve? The explicit gate (mint is total and safe without it). |
| `principal_current_name() -> str` | F3 (Phase 9): return the name of the principal currently active in the audit context. Returns "root" when none has been set via principal_activate. |
| `principal_holds(handle: i64, cap: str) -> bool` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 1): does the principal hold the named capability ("net"/"fs_write"/"exec")? Unknown name or handle → false (deny by default). |
| `principal_mint(parent: i64, name: str, net: bool, fs_write: bool, exec: bool, grant: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 1): mint an attenuated child of `parent` in the kernel registry. ATTENUATION BY CONSTRUCTION — child cap_X = want_X ∧ parent.X (escalation unrepresentable), grant clamped to the parent's remaining budget and carved from it. Returns the child handle; panics E1601 on an unknown parent handle. |
| `principal_root(name: str, net: bool, fs_write: bool, exec: bool, budget: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 1): register a ROOT principal — the originating authority — in the live kernel registry, holding exactly the given caps and full budget. Returns its handle (i64). Everything minted below it can only attenuate. |
| `principal_spend(handle: i64, amount: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 1): debit `amount` from the principal's own carved budget; returns the new remaining. Capabilities are untouched. |
| `print(msg: str) -> ()` | Write `msg` to stdout without a trailing newline. |
| `println(msg: str) -> ()` | Write `msg` to stdout followed by a newline. |
| `ptr_from_addr(addr: i64) -> i64` | R17 HAL: construct a raw pointer from a physical address (i64 since literals default to i64). Substrate-only (@[hal] required). Returns an opaque handle; pass to volatile_load/volatile_store. |
| `random_f64() -> f64` | Return a pseudo-random `f64` in `[0.0, 1.0)` (xorshift64). Reproducible via `srand`/`AXON_SEED`. |
| `random_i64(lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64` | Return a pseudo-random `i64` in `[lo, hi)` (xorshift64). Seed via `srand(n)` or the `AXON_SEED` env var for reproducible runs. Inverted bounds (`hi < lo`) panic — they're a caller error, not a silent degenerate. `hi == lo` returns `lo` (empty range). |
| `re_captures(pattern: str, s: str) -> Result<[str], str>` | Capture groups of the leftmost match: element 0 is the whole match, 1.. are the groups. Empty array when there is no match. A group that did not PARTICIPATE is reported as the empty string — indistinguishable from a group that matched empty, a documented limitation rather than a `[Option<str>]` return that complicates the common case to serve the rare one. NOTE: in a pattern literal, DOUBLE any braces (write a{{2,3}} not a{2,3}) — `{` opens string interpolation, and the single-brace form silently becomes a different pattern instead of erroring. |
| `re_find(pattern: str, s: str) -> Result<Option<str>, str>` | The leftmost match, or None. **Leftmost-FIRST (Perl/PCRE), not leftmost-longest:** `re_find("a\|ab", "ab")` is `"a"`, because alternation order is priority. Lazy quantifiers (`.*?`) therefore work as models expect. NOTE: in a pattern literal, DOUBLE any braces (write a{{2,3}} not a{2,3}) — `{` opens string interpolation, and the single-brace form silently becomes a different pattern instead of erroring. |
| `re_find_all(pattern: str, s: str) -> Result<[str], str>` | Every non-overlapping match, left to right. An empty match advances one character so the scan always terminates. NOTE: in a pattern literal, DOUBLE any braces (write a{{2,3}} not a{2,3}) — `{` opens string interpolation, and the single-brace form silently becomes a different pattern instead of erroring. |
| `re_is_match(pattern: str, s: str) -> Result<bool, str>` | Does `pattern` match anywhere in `s`? Result-returning because a pattern is DATA and may be malformed — a panic would be wrong for something a model composes at runtime. NOTE: in a pattern literal, DOUBLE any braces (write a{{2,3}} not a{2,3}) — `{` opens string interpolation, and the single-brace form silently becomes a different pattern instead of erroring. |
| `re_replace_all(pattern: str, s: str, with: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Replace every non-overlapping match. `with` interprets `$1`..`$9` as capture references and `$$` as a literal `$` — specified rather than left open, because two implementations would otherwise disagree later. NOTE: in a pattern literal, DOUBLE any braces (write a{{2,3}} not a{2,3}) — `{` opens string interpolation, and the single-brace form silently becomes a different pattern instead of erroring. |
| `re_split(pattern: str, s: str) -> Result<[str], str>` | Split `s` on every match of `pattern`. Adjacent matches yield empty fields, like every other split; a pattern that matches empty is refused rather than looping forever. NOTE: in a pattern literal, DOUBLE any braces (write a{{2,3}} not a{2,3}) — `{` opens string interpolation, and the single-brace form silently becomes a different pattern instead of erroring. |
| `read_file(path: str) -> Result<str, str>` | Read the entire contents of `path` as a UTF-8 string. Returns Ok(contents) or Err(message). |
| `read_line() -> str` | Read one line from stdin (without the trailing newline). Blocks until newline or EOF. |
| `round_f64(x: f64) -> f64` | Round `x` to the nearest integer, ties away from zero. |
| `sandbox_create(principal: i64, allowed_effects: str) -> i64` | F5 (Phase 9): register a runtime sandbox bound to `principal` that allows only the comma-separated `allowed_effects` (e.g. "AI,Net" or "IO" or ""). Returns a sandbox handle (i64). Interp-only (codegen E0910-refused). |
| `sandbox_create_scoped(principal: i64, allowed_effects: str, fs_read: str, fs_write: str, net: str) -> i64` | F5 + AUDIT T3: like `sandbox_create`, but the fs/net effects are restricted to comma-separated path prefixes and host globs. `""` DENIES everything on that axis; `"*"` is unrestricted; a list means every path/host must match an entry. Matches the `AXON_ALLOWED_EFFECTS` convention, where an empty value denies. Broad authority is stated explicitly (`"*"`) rather than implied by an empty list — see the capability-profile policy. Interp-only. |
| `sandbox_run(sandbox: i64, fn_name: str, arg: i64) -> i64` | F5 (Phase 9): call the named user function with `arg` inside the sandbox identified by `sandbox`. Any builtin that attempts an effect not declared in the sandbox ceiling raises a SandboxViolation (exit 8) and the call is refused. Returns the function's i64 result on success. Interp-only (codegen E0910-refused). |
| `scheduler_done_count() -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 2): how many fibers have completed successfully (the fan-out/collect summary). |
| `scheduler_failed(id: i64) -> bool` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 2): did the fiber fail (panic/halt during its run)? The signal the Slice-3 supervisor restarts on. |
| `scheduler_failed_count() -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 2): how many fibers have failed. |
| `scheduler_restart(id: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 2): re-queue a fiber as Ready so the next scheduler_run executes it again (the supervisor restart hook). Returns the id; no-op on an unknown id. |
| `scheduler_result(id: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 2): a completed fiber's i64 result (0 if it has not completed or the id is unknown). |
| `scheduler_run() -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 2): run all READY fibers to completion in the AXON_SEED-deterministic round-robin order; returns the count that completed successfully. A fiber that panics/halts is caught and marked failed (observable via scheduler_failed), NOT a process abort. Re-runnable — a restarted fiber runs on the next call. |
| `scheduler_spawn(fn_name: str, arg: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 2): queue a fiber — a call to the named user function with the given i64 arg (0-arg fns ignore it). Returns the fiber id. Panics E1602 if no such function exists. |
| `shl(n: i64, shift: i64) -> i64` | Left-shift `n` by `shift` bits (`n << shift`). |
| `shr(n: i64, shift: i64) -> i64` | Arithmetic right-shift `n` by `shift` bits (`n >> shift`). |
| `sign_i64(n: i64) -> i64` | Sign of `n`: -1, 0, or 1. |
| `sleep_ms(ms: i64) -> ()` | Suspend the current thread for at least `ms` milliseconds. |
| `sql_query(template: str, params: [str]) -> str` | Build a parameterized SQL query STRING. `template` MUST be a string literal — each `?` placeholder is filled, in order, by the next value in `params`, single-quoted with `'` doubled and `\` doubled. User-controlled data goes in `params`, NEVER in `template`: a template built by concatenation or interpolation is a compile error (E1210), which is what makes the query's STRUCTURE attacker-independent. SCOPE OF THE ESCAPING: it targets MySQL/MariaDB rules (backslash is an escape character). On a standard-conforming dialect (PostgreSQL, SQLite with standard_conforming_strings on) a backslash is a literal, so doubling it CORRUPTS the value — there, bind `params` through your driver instead of rendering them. This builtin renders text; it is not a substitute for driver-side parameter binding, and no amount of escaping is. Interpreter-only (codegen E0910-refused). |
| `sqrt(n: f64) -> f64` | Square root of `n`. Calls C sqrt; not comptime-evaluable. |
| `sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64` | Square root of `x`. |
| `srand(seed: i64) -> ()` | Seed the global RNG for reproducible runs. The same seed yields an identical sequence of `random_*` / `goal_run_random` / `goal_run_multistart` results. The `AXON_SEED` env var does the same without code changes. |
| `sti() -> ()` | R17 HAL: execute the x86_64 `sti` instruction — set interrupt flag (enable interrupts). Substrate-only. |
| `str_char_at(s: str, i: i64) -> str` | The `i`-th CHARACTER of `s` as a one-character string, or "" if `i` is out of range. Contrast `char_at`, which returns the `i`-th BYTE as an `i64` code unit — for non-ASCII text those are different positions and different values. |
| `str_char_slice(s: str, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> str` | Characters `lo`..`hi` of `s` (half-open), indexed by CHARACTER rather than by byte. Cannot split a character, so unlike `str_slice` it never refuses (E2200); out-of-range indices clamp. |
| `str_chars(s: str) -> [str]` | Split `s` into one one-character string per CHARACTER (Unicode scalar value, not grapheme cluster). The load-bearing character function: it turns per-character work into ordinary `arr_*` work over `[str]`, so `arr_group_by`/`dict_inc`/`arr_count_if` all apply. Prefer this over indexing in a loop — `str_len` counts BYTES, so a `while i < str_len(s)` loop over non-ASCII text does not iterate characters. |
| `str_cmp(a: str, b: str) -> i64` | Lexicographic byte-order comparison: -1 if `a` < `b`, 0 if equal, 1 if `a` > `b`. Drops directly into `arr_sort_by`, whose comparator is `fn(T, T) -> i64`. |
| `str_contains(s: str, needle: str) -> bool` | Return true if `s` contains `needle` as a substring. |
| `str_count(s: str, needle: str) -> i64` | Return the number of non-overlapping occurrences of `needle` in `s`. Returns 0 if `needle` is not found. An EMPTY needle matches at every char boundary, so `str_count(s, "")` is the char count plus one — both engines delegate to Rust's `str::matches`, which is where that convention comes from. |
| `str_digits_only(s: str) -> str` | Keep only the ASCII digits in `s`; everything else (dashes, spaces, letters, Unicode) is dropped. Composes with `parse_int`: `parse_int(str_digits_only("415-555-0142"))` → `Ok(4155550142)`. Closes ROADMAP §9.5 F7. |
| `str_ends_with(s: str, suffix: str) -> bool` | Return true if `s` ends with `suffix`. |
| `str_eq(a: str, b: str) -> bool` | Return true if `a` and `b` have the same content (byte-by-byte equality). |
| `str_index_of(s: str, needle: str) -> i64` | Return the byte index of the first occurrence of `needle` in `s`, or -1 if not found. |
| `str_join(parts: [str], sep: str) -> str` | Concatenate `parts` with `sep` between each. Inverse of `str_split`. Non-string elements panic; arr_map(to_str) first if needed. |
| `str_len(s: str) -> i64` | Return the byte length of `s`. |
| `str_len_chars(s: str) -> i64` | The number of CHARACTERS in `s`. Contrast `str_len`, which counts BYTES: `str_len("café")` is 5 and `str_len_chars("café")` is 4. |
| `str_pad_end(s: str, width: i64, fill: str) -> str` | Right-pad `s` with the first byte of `fill` until it is `width` bytes long. Returns `s` unchanged if already >= `width` bytes. |
| `str_pad_start(s: str, width: i64, fill: str) -> str` | Left-pad `s` with the first byte of `fill` until it is `width` bytes long. Returns `s` unchanged if already >= `width` bytes. |
| `str_repeat(s: str, n: i64) -> str` | Return a string containing `s` repeated `n` times (empty string if n <= 0). |
| `str_replace(s: str, from: str, to: str) -> str` | Return a copy of `s` with all non-overlapping occurrences of `from` replaced by `to`. |
| `str_reverse(s: str) -> str` | Return a copy of `s` with its bytes in reverse order. |
| `str_slice(s: str, start: i64, end: i64) -> str` | Return the substring of `s` from byte index `start` (inclusive) to `end` (exclusive). Clamps indices to valid range. |
| `str_split(s: str, sep: str) -> [str]` | Split `s` on every occurrence of `sep`, returning the parts as a slice. Empty separator returns `[s]` (avoids Rust's panic). Inverse of `str_join`. |
| `str_starts_with(s: str, prefix: str) -> bool` | Return true if `s` begins with `prefix`. |
| `str_to_lower(s: str) -> str` | Return a copy of `s` with all ASCII letters converted to lowercase. |
| `str_to_upper(s: str) -> str` | Return a copy of `s` with all ASCII letters converted to uppercase. |
| `str_trim(s: str) -> str` | Return `s` with leading and trailing ASCII whitespace removed. |
| `str_trim_end(s: str) -> str` | Return `s` with trailing ASCII whitespace removed. |
| `str_trim_start(s: str) -> str` | Return `s` with leading ASCII whitespace removed. |
| `supervisor_alive(sup: i64) -> bool` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 3): is the supervisor still running (not halted by a crash loop)? |
| `supervisor_new(strategy: i64, max_restarts: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 3): create a live supervisor (strategy 0=one_for_one, 1=one_for_all, 2=rest_for_one) with a max-restart intensity. Returns its handle. |
| `supervisor_restarts(sup: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 3): cumulative restart events the supervisor has observed. |
| `supervisor_run(sup: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 3): run the supervised fibers via the scheduler; on each failure restart the OTP strategy's set and re-run, until all children succeed OR the max-restart-intensity latch trips → HALT this subtree (exit 4). Returns the number of restart rounds performed. |
| `supervisor_supervise(sup: i64, fiber_id: i64) -> i64` | Phase-7 (R12 Slice 3): register a scheduler fiber as a supervised child (in start order). Returns its child index — the position restart strategies reason about. |
| `tee_attest_measurement() -> str` | R24 TEE: the enclave LAUNCH MEASUREMENT (a deterministic hash of the loaded image). SIMULATED locally (returns AXON_TEE_MEASUREMENT or a stub) — a genuine hardware-rooted attestation QUOTE is produced only on confidential hardware (tee.yml). |
| `tee_in_enclave() -> bool` | R24 TEE: true iff the workload is executing inside a TEE/enclave region. In the gramine-direct simulation this is signalled by the AXON_TEE_ENCLAVE=1 env var the manifest sets. (Runtime probe; the compile-time guarantee is the E1810 rule.) |
| `tee_seal(val: i64, level: i64) -> i64` | R24 TEE: seal a value at confidentiality `level` (0=public..3=secret). Sealing is allowed anywhere — only UNSEALING is enclave-gated. Returns the sealed payload (identity in the simulation; the type story is the Secret-lattice + E1810 rule). |
| `tee_unseal(sealed: i64, level: i64) -> i64` | R24 TEE: UNSEAL (declassify) a sealed Secret value INSIDE the enclave. May ONLY be called from within an `@[enclave]` fn — calling it outside an enclave context is E1810. This is the 'compute on data you can't read' boundary, enforced by types. |
| `temporal_at(t: Temporal<i64>, offset_ms: i64) -> Temporal<i64>` | Project `t` forward by `offset_ms` milliseconds, decaying confidence as c * (1 - decay)^(offset_ms / 86_400_000). |
| `temporal_confidence(t: Temporal<i64>) -> f64` | The present confidence of a `Temporal` value in [0,1] (PRD `rev.confidence`). Starts at 1.0 at creation and is decayed by `temporal_at` as time advances. Also readable as the `.confidence` field. |
| `temporal_is_valid(t: Temporal<i64>) -> bool` | Return true if `__axon_now_ms()` is still within the temporal value's validity window. |
| `temporal_new(value: i64, horizon_ms: i64, decay: f64) -> Temporal<i64>` | Construct a `Temporal<i64>` with a validity horizon (ms) and decay rate per day. |
| `temporal_now() -> i64` | Return the current validity timestamp for Temporal<T> values (milliseconds since epoch). |
| `to_str(n: i64) -> str` | Convert an `i64` to its decimal string representation. |
| `to_str_bool(b: bool) -> str` | Convert a bool to its string representation: "true" or "false". |
| `to_str_f64(n: f64) -> str` | Convert an `f64` to its string representation ("%.6g" format). |
| `uncertain_confidence(confidence: f64) -> ()` | A NO-OP confidence hint (0.0–1.0). It returns `()` and changes nothing: there is no "surrounding Uncertain<T>" for it to attach to, and no value already in scope has its confidence altered by calling it. Both engines discard the argument (interp returns `Value::Unit`; codegen emits an empty stub). To attach a confidence to a value, construct it with `uncertain_new` / `uncertain_new_f64` / `uncertain_dyn_i64` / `uncertain_dyn_f64`. |
| `uncertain_deterministic(value: i64) -> Uncertain<i64>` | Construct an `Uncertain<i64>` with confidence = 1.0 (deterministic value). |
| `uncertain_dyn_f64(value: f64, confidence: f64) -> Uncertain<f64>` | Same as uncertain_dyn_i64 but value is f64. |
| `uncertain_dyn_i64(value: i64, confidence: f64) -> Uncertain<i64>` | Construct an `Uncertain<i64>` from a runtime confidence value. Unlike `uncertain_new`, the static @[verify] checker classifies this as a Runtime source rather than Known — predicate decisions defer to the runtime check (__axon_verify_panic). Use this when confidence comes from runtime data (sensors, configs, computations) rather than literals. |
| `uncertain_new(value: i64, confidence: f64) -> Uncertain<i64>` | Construct an `Uncertain<i64>` with an explicit confidence in [0.0, 1.0]. |
| `uncertain_new_f64(value: f64, confidence: f64) -> Uncertain<f64>` | Construct an `Uncertain<f64>` with an explicit confidence in [0.0, 1.0]. |
| `volatile_load_u16(ptr: i64) -> i64` | R17 HAL: volatile load of a u16 from an MMIO address. Returns i64 (zero-extended). Substrate-only. |
| `volatile_load_u32(ptr: i64) -> i64` | R17 HAL: volatile load of a u32 from an MMIO address. Returns i64 (zero-extended). Substrate-only. |
| `volatile_load_u64(ptr: i64) -> i64` | R17 HAL: volatile load of a u64 from an MMIO address. Returns i64. Substrate-only. |
| `volatile_load_u8(ptr: i64) -> i64` | R17 HAL: volatile load of a u8 from an MMIO address (no optimizer elision). Returns i64 (zero-extended from u8). Substrate-only. |
| `volatile_store_u16(ptr: i64, val: i64) -> ()` | R17 HAL: volatile store of a u16 (truncated from i64) to an MMIO address. Substrate-only. |
| `volatile_store_u32(ptr: i64, val: i64) -> ()` | R17 HAL: volatile store of a u32 (truncated from i64) to an MMIO address. Substrate-only. |
| `volatile_store_u64(ptr: i64, val: i64) -> ()` | R17 HAL: volatile store of a u64 to an MMIO address. Substrate-only. |
| `volatile_store_u8(ptr: i64, val: i64) -> ()` | R17 HAL: volatile store of a u8 (truncated from i64) to an MMIO address. Substrate-only. |
| `wrapping_add(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Add two i64 with two's-complement wraparound instead of the checked `+`'s overflow panic. |
| `wrapping_div(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Divide two i64, wrapping on the one overflowing case: `wrapping_div(i64::MIN, -1)` is `i64::MIN`. Division by ZERO still panics — zero has no wrapped quotient. |
| `wrapping_mul(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Multiply two i64 with two's-complement wraparound instead of the checked `*`'s overflow panic. |
| `wrapping_rem(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Remainder of two i64. `wrapping_rem(i64::MIN, -1)` is 0 (a representable answer; the pair is special only because x86 `idiv` traps on it). Remainder by ZERO still panics. |
| `wrapping_sub(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` | Subtract two i64 with two's-complement wraparound instead of the checked `-`'s overflow panic. |
| `write_file(path: str, content: str) -> Result<(), str>` | Write `content` to `path`, creating or truncating the file. Returns Ok(()) or Err(message). |
| `zephyr_console_putc(byte: i64) -> ()` | R25 HAL: write one byte to the Zephyr console by calling the host-provided extern C hook `axon_console_putc(int)` (e.g. a `printk` wrapper). Architecture-neutral — used when an Axon object links into a Zephyr app on ARM Cortex-M / RISC-V / x86. Substrate-only; codegen-only (E0910 in interp). |
